title: Thank you, baby: shout-outs for the small things
summary: A quick, slightly sappy thank-you list for the people and little things that make life better. AI helps you turn vague thanks into short, specific lines.
why: A weekly social media trends roundup published October 28, 2026 lists "Thank You Baby" in its October 21 section: creators use a catchy thank-you audio to spotlight things they're grateful for, like a partner who does the dishes or a friend with great food tips.
steps: Jot down a few people and small things you're grateful for this week.
Use the main prompt to turn them into short, specific thank-you lines.
Film a quick clip for each line, or one clip with the lines appearing in turn, and add the trending thank-you sound from the app.
Tag the people you thanked, if they're happy to be in it.

prompts.label: Main prompt
prompts.text: Help me make a short gratitude video. Turn this list into 6 thank-you lines for on-screen text, each under 10 words, each starting with "Thank you". Make them specific and a little sappy, not generic. Here's what I'm grateful for: [your list, for example: my partner doing the dishes, my friend who always picks the restaurant, my dog waiting at the door]. No hashtags, no emojis.

prompts.label: Variation: funny version
prompts.text: Write 8 short, funny thank-you lines for on-screen text, each under 10 words, thanking small everyday things as if they were heroes. For example the last clean mug, a green light when I'm late, or my phone at 1 per cent hanging on. Keep it warm and silly.

prompts.label: Variation: a note to send
prompts.text: I want to send a short thank-you message to [who] for [what they did]. Write 3 versions under 50 words each: one heartfelt, one funny, one that fits in a text. Mention the specific thing they did and how it helped me. Plain words, no clichés.

prompts.label: Variation: small business
prompts.text: I run [your type of business] in [your town]. Write 8 thank-you lines for a short video, each under 10 words, where our team thanks real groups of people: regulars, first-time visitors, our suppliers, our staff, people who share our posts. Mention real things we do, like [one or two examples]. Warm, not salesy. Don't make up customer names, numbers, reviews or deals.

tips: Specific beats general. "Thank you for always saving me the window seat" hits harder than "thanks for everything".
Ask before you tag or film someone you're thanking.
Keep each line on screen long enough to read: about two seconds.
Businesses: thank groups, not invented customers. Never make up quotes or numbers.
